citations.title: On the difference between clique partition and clique covering numbers
The difference between the clique numbers of a graph

evidence: The covering number hℓ is forced by choosing one representative from each cluster on both sides, which induces K_{h,ℓ}; any graph clique contains representatives from at most one cluster on each side and thus covers at most one selected crossing edge.

The Erdős–Faudree–Ordman cut inequality yields cp(G)>=s-2a-b because the load hypothesis implies a<=b. The modular assignment of each first-side internal edge to a B-cluster is injective within each A-row and globally balanced, so K4 pairings are edge-disjoint and within the stated capacity.

After those K4s, each remaining B-internal edge fits into a distinct unused A_i–B_j pair because e_j<=C(q+1,2)<=h; triangles therefore do not reuse crossing edges. Counting K4s, triangles, and leftover 2-cliques gives exactly s-2a-b.

The asymptotic choice was recomputed: the three n^(4/3) terms are c/2, 1/(4 sqrt(c)), and 1/(4 sqrt(c)); c=2^(-2/3) equalizes them and yields 3/2^(5/3). Lower-order remainder terms do not affect the limsup.

limitations: The capacity hypotheses are sufficient rather than necessary, and the constant 3/2^(5/3) is not claimed optimal.
Very recent or differently phrased clique-decomposition literature remains a residual originality risk.

evidence: Ning's 2026 preprint establishes d_n=Theta(n^(4/3)) and uses a balanced uniform cluster-join family; the heterogeneous q/q+1 correction and the displayed all-order coefficient are not stated in the checked direct source.

The cut lower bound itself is correctly attributed to Erdős–Faudree–Ordman and is not claimed as new. Targeted searches under clique partition/cover, cluster joins, and cograph/decomposition terminology did not locate the same finite exactness theorem.
The mixed family removes isolated-vertex padding and gives a reusable finite exactness criterion plus an explicit quantitative second-order constant within the known Theta(n^(4/3)) deficit scale.
